Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 2–3:

﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."﴾ That is: passing away, and it will pass and vanish. From their saying: "The matter passed (marra)" and "it continued (istamarra)" when it went away, like their saying: "it settled (qarra)" and "it became settled (istaqarra)." This is the statement of Mujahid and Qatadah. Abu al-'Aliyah [and al-Dahhak] [[Omitted from "b".]] said: "mustamirr" means: strong and severe, overpowering every magic, from their saying: "the rope became firm (marra al-habl)" when it became hard and strong, and "I made it firm (amrartuhu)" when I twisted it tightly, and "the matter became continuous (istamarra al-shay')" when it grew strong and well-established.

﴿And they denied and followed their desires﴾ That is: they denied the Prophet (ﷺ) and what they witnessed of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they followed what Satan had made attractive to them of falsehood.

﴿And every matter is settled﴾ Al-Kalbi said: every matter has a reality; what was of it in this world will become manifest, and what was of it in the Hereafter will be known. Qatadah said: every matter is settled: good is settled with the people of good, [and evil is settled with the people of evil] [[The words between the brackets are an addition from "b".]].

It was also said: every matter, whether good or evil, has a settled outcome: good is settled with its people in Paradise, and evil is settled with its people in the Fire.

It was also said: the statements of those who affirm and those who deny will settle, until they know its reality through reward and punishment. Muqatil said: every report has an end. It was also said: whatever has been decreed will certainly come to pass.

Abu Ja'far read "mustaqirrin" with a kasra on the ra', and there is no basis for it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verses 8–13:

﴿Muhti'in﴾ (hastening, coming forward eagerly) to ﴿the caller﴾, to the sound of Israfil. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a hard day."﴾ A difficult, severe day.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Before them, the people of Nuh denied﴾, meaning: before the people of Makkah. ﴿They denied Our servant﴾, Nuh, ﴿and said, "A madman," and he was rebuked.﴾ Meaning: they drove him away from his call and his message with insults and threats, and they said, "If you do not desist, O Nuh, you will surely be among those stoned" [al-Shu'ara: 116]. Mujahid said that the meaning of ﴿uzdujira﴾ is: he was driven mad (istutira jununan).

﴿So he called﴾ upon ﴿his Lord﴾ and said, ﴿"I am overpowered, so help [me]"﴾, meaning: defeated, so take vengeance for me against them.

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾, poured down with a severe downpour that did not stop for forty days. Yaman said: it covered everything between the heaven and the earth.

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, and the waters met﴾, meaning the water of the sky and the water of the earth. He said "the waters met" although meeting does not happen with one thing; it happens between two or more, since the water can be both a collective noun and a singular. ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari read: "fa-iltaqa al-māān" (the two waters met).

﴿According to a matter already decreed﴾, meaning: it had been decided against them in the Mother of the Book. Muqatil said: God had decreed that the two waters would be equal, so they were as He had decreed.

﴿And We carried him﴾, meaning Nuh, ﴿upon a [vessel] of planks and nails﴾, meaning a ship with planks. He mentioned the attribute and omitted the noun. By "planks" he meant the wide wooden boards of the ship. ﴿Nails﴾ means the pegs with which the planks are fastened; its singular is dissar and dasir. It is said: "dasartu al-safina" when one fastens the ship with nails. Al-Hasan said: ﴿dusur﴾ is the prow of the ship, so called because it thrusts (tudassir) the water with its breast, meaning it pushes. Mujahid said: they are the ribs of the ship. It was also said: its ribs. Al-Dahhak said: the planks are its sides, and the nails are its base and its ends.

﴿ʿĀd denied, so how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ **Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind**, **shadīdat al-hubūb** (severe in its blowing), **﴿on a day of ill omen, continuing﴾**, meaning severe and perpetually inauspicious. **﴿plucking up people﴾** (tanziʿu al-nās), meaning it uprooted them, then hurled them down on their heads so that their necks broke. It is narrated that it used to pluck people out of their graves. **﴿as though they were trunks of palm trees﴾** (aʿjāzu nakhl). Ibn ʿAbbās said: their roots. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: their trunks.

**﴿So how was My punishment and My warning? And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?﴾** **﴿Thamūd denied the warnings﴾**, meaning the warning that Ṣāliḥ brought them.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them﴾, a test and a examination for them, ﴿so watch them﴾, meaning wait and see what they will do, ﴿and be patient﴾, meaning be patient over their waiting. It was said: be patient over the harm that befalls you.

﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them﴾, between them and the she-camel: one day for her and one day for them. He said "between them" because when the Arabs speak about the children of Adam and about animals together, they give precedence to the children of Adam over the animals. ﴿Every share of water is to be attended﴾, meaning every portion of water is attended by whoever has his turn. When it is her day, she comes to her share, and when it is their day, they come to their share. *Haḍara* and *iḥtaḍara* have the same meaning. Mujahid said: it means they would come to the water when the she-camel was absent, and when the she-camel came they would come to the milk.

﴿So they called their companion﴾, and he was Qidar ibn Salif, ﴿so he took up [the sword]﴾, meaning he took the she-camel with his sword, ﴿and hamstrung her﴾, meaning he hamstrung her.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ Then He explained their punishment, saying:

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 54, verses 38–45:**

﴿And verily, a lasting punishment came to them early in the morning.﴾ It came to them at the time of dawn. ﴿A lasting punishment﴾: constant, abiding, settling upon them until it led them to the punishment of the Hereafter. It was also said: "a true punishment."

﴿So taste My punishment and warnings. And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? And there certainly came to the family of Pharaoh the warnings.﴾ It means Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both. It was also said: they are the signs with which Musa warned them.

﴿They denied all Our signs﴾, which were the nine signs. ﴿So We seized them﴾ with punishment, ﴿with the seizure of One Almighty﴾, Overpowering in His retribution, ﴿Omnipotent﴾, Able to destroy them, whom nothing He wills can frustrate. Then he warned the people of Makkah, saying:

﴿Are your disbelievers better than those? Or do you have immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ Are they stronger and more powerful than those upon whom I brought down My vengeance, from the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, and the family of Pharaoh? This is a rhetorical question meaning denial, i.e., they are not stronger than them. ﴿Or do you have immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ The punishment, ﴿in the Zubur﴾, in the books, that it will never befall you as it befell the earlier nations.

﴿Or do they say: "We are a united host, victorious"?﴾ It means the disbelievers of Makkah. Al-Kalbi said: "We are a united force of our affair, victorious [over] our enemies." The meaning is: "We are one hand against whoever opposes us, victorious over whoever is hostile to us." He did not say "victorious" in the plural (munتصirun) in order to match the rhyme endings (ra'us al-aya).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The host will be routed and they will turn their backs.﴾ Ya'qub recited "sa-nahzimu" with the letter nun, and "al-jam'a" in the accusative. The others recited it with the letter ya' and a damma on it, with "al-jam'u" in the nominative, in the passive voice, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And they will turn their backs﴾.

It means "al-adbar" (the backs), and he used the singular for the sake of the rhyme endings, as it is said: "We struck the heads among them" and "We struck the head among them," when the singular conveys the meaning of the plural. Allah informed that they would turn their backs in flight, so Allah fulfilled His promise and defeated them on the Day of Badr.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ), while he was in his tent on the Day of Badr, said: "O Allah, I implore You for Your covenant and Your promise. O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped after today." Abu Bakr took his hand and said: "That is enough, O Messenger of Allah, for you have pressed upon your Lord," while he was wearing his armour. So he went out saying: "The host will be routed and they will turn their backs." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on what was said about the armour and shirt of the Prophet (ﷺ) in war: 6/99, and in al-Maghazi, and in al-Tafsir; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/400.] [In "a" it reads "mustaqirr" (مستقر).]

**Indeed the criminals** (the polytheists) **are in error and madness.** It was said: "in error" means distance from the truth. Al-Dahhak said: "and madness" means fire that is kindled against them. It was also said: "error" means straying from the path to Paradise in the Hereafter, and "madness" means a kindled fire. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The criminals are in error in this world and in fire in the Hereafter. Qatadah said: in toil and punishment. [[See al-Tabari (27/109).]]

Then He explained their punishment, saying: **"On the Day they will be dragged into the Fire upon their faces,"** and it will be said to them, **"Taste the touch of Saqar."**

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 49:

﴿Indeed, We have created everything in measure.﴾ That is: whatever We have created is predestined and written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Al-Hasan said: Allah has determined for each of His creatures the measure that befits it.

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qurashi informed us, Abu Muslim Ghalib ibn Ali al-Razi informed us, Abu [Ma'shar] [[In "A" it is "Mash'ar," and the correct reading is what we have written, from "B."]] Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Jalil ibn Ya'qub informed us, Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub related to us, Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Nisaburi informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Adani informed us, al-Thawri informed us from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Muhammad ibn Abbad al-Makhzumi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ disputing with him about divine decree (al-qadar), and this verse was revealed: "Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness," up to His saying: "Indeed, We have created everything in measure." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Divine Decree, chapter "Everything is by measure," no. (2656): 4/2046, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/150.]]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi'i al-Khudhashahi informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jawarbadhi informed us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la al-Sadafi informed us, Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Hani' al-Khawlani informed me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman [al-Hubuli] [[In "A" it is "al-Jibli," which is a copyist's error.]], from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah wrote the measures of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." He said: "And His Throne was upon the water." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Divine Decree, chapter on the disputation of Adam and Musa, peace be upon them, no. (2653): 4/2044, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/123.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us from Malik, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said: I met people from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who used to say: "Everything is by the decree of Allah." He said: I also heard Abd Allah ibn [Umar] [[In "B" it is "Amr," and the correct reading is what we have written.]], may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Everything is by measure, even incapacity and capability, or capability and incapacity." [[Narrated by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Divine Decree, chapter on the prohibition of speaking about qadar: 2/899; Muslim in the Book of Divine Decree, chapter "Everything is by measure," no. (2655): 4/2045; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/134.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaym al-Shaybani informed us, Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharazah informed us, Ya'la ibn Ubayd, and [Ubayd Allah] [[In "A" it is "Abd Allah," and the correct reading is what we have written.]] ibn Musa and Abu Nu'aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ribi ibn Hirash, from a man, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, whom He sent with the truth; he believes in resurrection after death [147/a]; and he believes in divine decree (al-qadar)." [Ubayd Allah] [[In "A" it is "Abd Allah," and the correct reading is what we have written.]] added: "its good and its evil." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Divine Decree, chapter on what has come that belief in qadar, its good and its evil: 6/358; Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. (23), p. 37; Imam Ahmad: 1/233; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/122.]]

Abu Dawud related it from Shu'bah, from Mansur, and said: from Ribi, from Ali, and he did not say "from a man." This is more authentic. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi 1/22 (106), and through him al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Divine Decree, chapter on what has come concerning belief in qadar, its good and its evil: 6/357; Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on qadar, no. (81): 1/32; Ibn Abi Asim: 1/59; al-Lalaka'i in Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunnah: 3/620; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/32, and al-Dhahabi agreed; Imam Ahmad: 1/97. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 1/122. See: Sahih al-Jami' al-Saghir wa Ziyadatuh, no. (7584).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 50–53:

﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.﴾ ﴿Wāḥidatun﴾ (one). It refers to the meaning rather than the wording, i.e., "Our command is but one time."

It was also said: its meaning is: "Our command concerning a thing, when We intend to bring it into being, is but one word: 'Be,' and it is, without any reversal, like a glance of the eye." ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbas: He means that My decree concerning My creation is swifter than the glance of the eye. Al-Kalbi related from him: Our command regarding the coming of the Hour, in speed, is only like the blink of the eye.

﴿And We have certainly destroyed your counterparts﴾, i.e., your likes and peers in disbelief, from the past nations.

﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ i.e., one who takes heed, knows that this is true, and so fears and takes a lesson.

﴿And everything they have done is in the Zubur﴾, i.e., what their counterparts did of good and evil, ﴿in the Zubur﴾, in the book of the recording angels. It was also said: in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿And every small and great matter﴾ of the creation, their deeds and their terms (of life), ﴿is inscribed﴾, i.e., written down. It is said: sattara and istatara, and kataba and iktataba (all meaning "to write").

Verse 54–55: "Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers."

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens﴾ — bustans (orchards). ﴿and rivers﴾ — i.e., rivers (the singular is used for the sake of the rhyme endings, āy). He meant the rivers of Paradise: of water, wine, milk and honey.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it means in brightness and expanse, and from this comes the word nahār (daytime).

Al-A'raj read "wa-nuhurin" with two ḍammahs, the plural of nahār (day), meaning: a day in which they will have no night.

﴿In a seat of truth﴾ — in an assembly of truth, free of idle talk and sinful speech, ﴿in the presence of a sovereign, All-Powerful﴾ — a King who is capable, whom nothing can overpower.

Ja'far al-Ṣādiq said: God praised the place with truthfulness, so no one sits in it except the people of truth.
